summary: Clinch County tower recorded in a Georgia tower list (GFC 825); no source found describes its build, staffing or fate.

evidence.supports: Clinch County; coordinates; elevation 140 (the list gives no unit); GFC number 825
column headers: elevation with no unit given
NHLR lists 29 Georgia lookouts; the full list of 29 names has no Spooner
evidence.quote: There are 29 lookouts registered in Georgia.

evidence.supports: FFLOS lists two Georgia former sites (Lafayette, Yonah Mountain), neither at Spooner
evidence.quote: There are 2 former lookout sites registered in Georgia.

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence. The only source for this tower is the tnlandforms list: coordinates, elevation and GFC number 825. The list's column headers name the elevation without a unit. The record's elevation_m of 42.7 matches 140 ft, so the story reads the figure as feet and says so. The same page says GFC provided coordinates for 118 towers (BLL-nnn) and an older GFC list covers 203 towers (gfc-nnn); the story gives the codes without expanding them. Nothing found on build, staffing, fate or the site today. The story is about 110 words, under the 120-word guide floor, on purpose: padding would not be honest. A 2026 Spooner Road wildfire in Clinch County appeared in searches (Watch Duty, local news); it is unrelated to the tower and not used. The NHLR and FFLOS counts come from the local crawl copy, not a live check; that copy's full NHLR list has 29 names and no Spooner, and its two FFLOS sites are Lafayette and Yonah Mountain. Fact-check 2026-10-21: removed the US that had been added to the GFC reference (the list reads gfc-825), replaced the unlabelled feet figure with a stated reading, added the missing footnote to the first sentence, and narrowed 'No source describes' to the sources read. The Tom Dunigan credit is not on the Georgia page; it comes from the same site's Tennessee page footer.
